newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Dublin air passenger traffic up 13pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Dublin air passenger traffic up 13pct in 1996.

text.p: Passenger traffic at Dublin airport rose 13 percent to nearly 9.1 million in 1996, according to preliminary year-end figures released by Irish airport authority Aer Rianta on Tuesday.
Aer Rianta said in a statement that last year was Dublin airport's busiest year ever.
It said there was 15 percent growth on routes to and from Britain and nine percent growth on routes to the continent.

Transatlantic routes enjoyed growth of 19 percent, transit traffic was up by 68 percent while domestic traffic also contributed to the good performance with an increase of seven percent, the company said.
Aer Rianta said the month of December was a particularly busy month in 1996 with 603,316 passengers using Dublin airport, a 10 percent improvement on the previous year.
Passanger records were also broken at Cork and Shannon airports, it said.
Aer Rianta said Cork broke the one million passenger barrier for the first time, showing 16 percent growth to 1.12 million passangers in 1996.
It said Shannon showed an 11 percent increase in traffic for 1996 with throughput figures of 1.74 passengers.
